REClassic350.architecturePrinciple: Long Wheelbase Impact on Comfort vs. Agility
REClassic350.description: The Classic 350's extended wheelbase (1,395 mm) is a deliberate design choice to optimize for comfort and stability at highway speeds, sacrificing low-speed agility.

architecturalDetails.frameType: Cradle frame with single central spine

modificationImplications.consequence: Front end becomes lighter; more responsive steering; improved damping reduces chatter

comparativeAnalysis.principalDifference: Classic 350 has long wheelbase (1,395mm) with steep rake (29°) for stability; RE 650 is longer (1,465mm) with moderate rake (26°) for sport-cruise; KTM 200 is short (1,357mm) with shallow rake (25°) for agility

REClassic350.architecturePrinciple: Cradle Frame Stiffness Limitations & Load Path Characteristics
REClassic350.description: The Classic 350 uses a traditional cradle frame with engine cradle and central spine tubes, which provides simplicity but creates load path limitations at frame lugs and welded joints.

howItManifests.boardRiskFactors: Frame fatigue risk if subjected to constant heavy loading beyond design envelope

modificationImplications.consequence: Increases dynamic loads 15-20%; stress concentrates at cradle lugs

modificationImplications.consequence: Changes rear frame load distribution; reduces frame twisting
modificationImplications.reasonForConsequence: Monoshock eliminates dual-shock frame unbalance

modificationImplications.consequence: Increases fork load 30%; transfers braking force through steering head

comparativeAnalysis.principalDifference: Classic 350 has basic single cradle (6-8 critical welds); Himalayan 411 has duplex cradle with reinforcement (12-14 reinforced welds)
comparativeAnalysis.whyPrincipleDiffers: Himalayan needs off-road load capability; multiple load paths provide redundancy
comparativeAnalysis.performanceImpact: Himalayan better for adventure riding and asymmetric loads; Classic 350 better for symmetrical highway touring

REClassic350.engineeringRationale: Cradle frame design prioritizes simplicity and cost; engine mounts at four points; load concentration at lugs limits modification potential

REClassic350.architecturePrinciple: Rake Angle Trade-off: Stability vs. Steering Response
REClassic350.description: The Classic 350's steeper rake angle (~29°) prioritizes straight-line stability and highway cruise comfort, but compromises steering agility. This is a fundamental design choice.

RE650.description: The RE 650's parallel-twin engine creates higher unbalanced masses compared to single-cylinder bikes. The duplex cradle frame routes loads around the engine, preventing resonance transmission.

howItManifests.ridingFeeling: Smooth power delivery; minimal vibration through pegs; handlebars receive 60% less vibration than equivalent single-cylinder

modificationImplications.consequence: Increases inertial forces 15%; vibration increases despite smoother balance

modificationImplications.consequence: Transmits engine vibration directly to frame; increases handlebar buzz

modificationImplications.consequence: Increases primary mass; makes rev-matching smoother

RE650.architecturePrinciple: Duplex Cradle Frame Load Distribution in 650cc Displacement

howItManifests.boardRiskFactors: Torsional stiffness ~6.8 Hz prevents resonance with engine operating frequencies

modificationImplications.consequence: Changes suspension force geometry; duplex frame handles shock loads well

modificationImplications.consequence: Adds lateral asymmetric loads; duplex frame better distributes than single-cradle

modificationImplications.consequence: Concentrates loads at rear frame lugs; duplex cradle handles well

comparativeAnalysis.whyPrincipleDiffers: 650's heavier displacement needs more balanced loading; Classic's simplicity trades load distribution for cost
comparativeAnalysis.performanceImpact: 650 better for heavy touring loads; Classic lighter and simpler but limited for passenger + luggage

Himalayan411.architecturePrinciple: Adventure Frame Geometry: Longer Wheelbase for Stability & Ground Clearance Trade-off

CrossPlatform.architecturePrinciple: Frame Type Determines Modification Envelope: Cradle vs. Trellis
CrossPlatform.description: The frame type fundamentally determines what modifications are possible. Cradle frames can tolerate engine displacement increases with bracing; trellis frames are already optimized and can't absorb further stiffness.

howItManifests.ridingFeeling: Varies by frame type and modification choice
howItManifests.handlingCharacteristic: Frame type is fundamental constraint on modifications
howItManifests.performanceImplication: Cradle frames allow diverse modification paths; trellis frames restricted
howItManifests.boardRiskFactors: Understanding frame type is critical for modification planning

modificationImplications.modificationType: Engine displacement increase on cradle frame
modificationImplications.consequence: Possible with reinforcement; frame has load distribution redundancy
modificationImplications.reasonForConsequence: Cradle frames allow bracing to accommodate larger displacement
modificationImplications.mitigationStrategy: Feasible up to ~90cc increase with proper reinforcement

CrossPlatform.architecturePrinciple: Rake Angle vs. Wheelbase: Why Different Platforms Handle Differently
CrossPlatform.description: Rake angle and wheelbase work together to create handling character. It's not one or the other—it's the combination that determines overall chassis character.

howItManifests.ridingFeeling: Combination of rake and wheelbase creates overall character
howItManifests.handlingCharacteristic: Long wheelbase + steep rake = stable cruiser; short wheelbase + shallow rake = agile sport
howItManifests.performanceImplication: No single parameter defines handling; interaction of multiple factors critical
howItManifests.boardRiskFactors: Modifying one parameter without considering the other creates imbalance

modificationImplications.modificationType: Changing rake angle without adjusting wheelbase
modificationImplications.consequence: Creates handling imbalance; corner entry vs. midcorner feel mismatched
modificationImplications.reasonForConsequence: Rake and wheelbase are fundamentally coupled in handling
modificationImplications.mitigationStrategy: Avoid solo rake changes; modify as integrated geometry

modificationImplications.consequence: Requires suspension tuning to rebalance handling
modificationImplications.reasonForConsequence: Trail change affects rake + wheelbase equilibrium
modificationImplications.mitigationStrategy: Suspension adjustments necessary after trail-changing modifications

modificationImplications.consequence: Makes turning-in slower; affects corner speed
modificationImplications.reasonForConsequence: Wheelbase change alters fundamental handling balance
modificationImplications.mitigationStrategy: Not recommended; verify desired handling changes before modifying

modificationImplications.modificationType: Integrated geometry tuning (rake + wheelbase + trail together)
modificationImplications.consequence: Can optimize handling for specific use case
modificationImplications.reasonForConsequence: Holistic approach respects fundamental coupling
modificationImplications.mitigationStrategy: Expert-level tuning; requires understanding of complete geometry

comparativeAnalysis.principalDifference: All platforms show rake + wheelbase + trail working together: Classic 350 (29°+1395mm=stable), RE 650 (26°+1465mm=sport-cruise), Himalayan (27°+1510mm=stable-explorer), KTM 200 (25°+1357mm=quick), KTM 390 (27°+1480mm=agile-adventure)
comparativeAnalysis.whyPrincipleDiffers: Each platform optimizes rake + wheelbase combination for intended use case
comparativeAnalysis.performanceImpact: Combination creates handling character; no single parameter defines it

CrossPlatform.engineeringRationale: Rake angle + wheelbase + trail form integrated system. Changing one requires compensating changes in others to maintain handling balance.
